item.title: Free Local Dictation That Works Everywhere
item.description:
Part 1 of 1 · AI in my workflow
  1. Free Local Dictation That Works Everywhere

The problem

Working with AI tools means a lot of typing: in chat apps, coding assistants, the browser and the terminal. For long prompts, speaking is faster than typing. The dictation in Claude and ChatGPT is very good, but it only works inside those apps, and not always there either. For example, it doesn’t work in the Claude Code extension for VS Code when VS Code is connected to a remote machine over SSH.

The other options on Windows are weaker:

  • Windows voice typing (Win + H) works in every app, but it makes many more mistakes than the dictation in the chat apps.
  • The GitHub Copilot app (hold Ctrl + Space) uses a small model, NVIDIA’s nemotron-speech-streaming-en-0.6b. It runs on the CPU, and you can’t change the model.

The goal is one dictation tool for the whole computer that types into whatever window is active. It should also be free, with no subscription and no word limit.

Such a tool has two parts. The model turns speech into text: Whisper (from OpenAI) is the most widely used, and Parakeet (from NVIDIA) is its main competitor. The app handles the shortcut key, records your voice and pastes the text.

Handy: free, offline, open source

Handy is a free, open-source app (MIT license) for Windows, macOS and Linux. You hold a shortcut key, speak, and release it. Handy then pastes the text where the cursor is. Everything runs on your own computer, and you choose the model.

Among the free, open-source apps for Windows, Handy is by far the most popular:

Star counts on 7 November 2026. Stars only give a rough idea of popularity.
App GitHub stars License First release
Handy 37,865 MIT Jun 2025
OpenWhispr 10,910 MIT Jul 2025
CapsWriter-Offline 7,083 MIT May 2023
Whispering (Epicenter) 4,840 unclear Mar 20231
Amical 1,599 MIT Jul 2025

The best-known dictation app, Wispr Flow, runs in the cloud and is not fully free. Its results often feel better than plain Whisper or Parakeet because it also cleans up the text with AI, but the free plan allows only about 2,000 words a week (after that it slows down, with a hard limit at 5,000 words).2 Since both apps work the same way, one option is to use Wispr Flow until the limit, then switch to Handy.

Setup takes a few minutes:

  1. Install Handy from a terminal with winget install cjpais.Handy, or download it from handy.computer.
  2. In the settings, download a model: Whisper large-v3-turbo if the computer has a GPU, or Parakeet V3 if it only has a CPU.
  3. Choose a shortcut key that other apps don’t already use. For example, Copilot uses Ctrl + Space.

Does Handy really use the GPU?

The test machine is a laptop with two GPUs: a built-in Intel GPU and an NVIDIA RTX PRO 500 (6 GB memory, 40 W). handy.exe shows up in nvidia-smi, but that only means the app draws its window on the GPU. To check if the model itself runs on the GPU, measure the GPU once per second while dictating:

1..75 | % { nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,memory.used --format=csv,noheader; Start-Sleep 1 }

The results show a clear pattern:

  • While speaking: the GPU is at 0% and uses 0 MiB of memory. Handy only records.
  • After releasing the key: the GPU works at 91% for about 1 second, and memory goes from 0 to about 1 GB. This is the model loading and transcribing.
  • A little later: the memory is free again, because Handy unloads the model when it isn’t in use.

What this means:

  • “Speed” is the waiting time after you stop talking. Whisper-type models transcribe the whole recording in one go. On this GPU the wait is about one second, which feels instant.
  • Model size decides the memory use, not the length of the recording. Speaking longer takes more time, not more memory.
  • Bigger models fit in memory, but they are slower. Handy rates Mistral’s Voxtral Mini 3B better for English. It is about three times bigger, so each phrase could take around 3–4 seconds on this GPU. This is an estimate and hasn’t been measured yet.

Recommended setup

Handy with Whisper large-v3-turbo on an NVIDIA GPU: free, offline, no word limit, about one second per phrase, and it works in every app. The text is less polished than Wispr Flow’s, but for prompts to an AI it is good enough.

Footnotes

  1. This date is for the whole Epicenter repository, which contains more than Whispering. Whispering itself was launched on Hacker News in August 2025.↩︎

  2. From Wispr Flow’s documentation in November 2026. The limits can change at any time.↩︎

NoteDummy post

This is a placeholder article to show how a series looks. Replace or delete it.

The idea

A star schema puts one big fact table (events you measure, like sales) in the middle, surrounded by small dimension tables (who, what, where, when).

Table Example columns
fact_sales date_id, product_id, store_id, quantity, revenue
dim_product product_id, name, category, brand
dim_store store_id, city, country
dim_date date_id, day, month, year, is_holiday

A query

SELECT d.year, p.category, SUM(f.revenue) AS revenue
FROM fact_sales f
JOIN dim_date d    ON f.date_id = d.date_id
JOIN dim_product p ON f.product_id = p.product_id
GROUP BY d.year, p.category;
